10005397.bio: Audrey Mika is an American pop singer who broke through in 2020 with "Y U Gotta B Like That" featuring KYLE from the 5 A.M. EP. Her bright pop mixes R&B textures and dance-electronic undercurrents, with collaborations alongside Gryffin and Young Bombs.
10005397.name: Audrey MiKa

10041822.bio: Mexican singer and a leading figure of corridos tumbados, adding trap beats and rapping to regional Mexican folk songs. Collaborated with Peso Pluma; Porque La Demora (2025) is among his recent releases.
10041822.name: Natanael Cano

10052.bio: Blur are an English band from London, formed in 1988, and key figures of 1990s Britpop. They combined glam, new wave and art-rock, then turned toward lo-fi and experimental sounds. Key records include Parklife (1994), Blur (1997) and The Ballad of Darren (2023).
10052.name: Blur

10060426.bio: Madeline Johnston is a self-taught multi-instrumentalist and engineer from Denver, now in southern Colorado. Midwife makes slow, heavy, ghostly shoegaze-slowcore; recent records are No Depression in Heaven (2024) and Never Die (2025).
10060426.name: Midwife

10108090.bio: Dominican rapper from Santo Domingo, emerging in the late 2010s with a hedonistic take on trap and dembow. Her 2021 breakthrough came with J Balvin on Perra and Rosalía on Linda; latest release AMOR & DROGA (2026).
10108090.name: Tokischa

10108270.bio: Las Vegas-born rapper, producer and songwriter, cousin of Kendrick Lamar, who rose with the mixtape Die for My Bitch (2019). His genre-shifting, off-kilter approach continued on The Melodic Blue (2021) and Ca$ino (2026).
10108270.name: Baby Keem

10163870.bio: Stray Fossa is a Charlottesville-formed trio, now partly based in Germany, playing dreamy surf-tinged indie rock. They released Closer Than We'll Ever Know (2022) and Blossomer (2025).
10163870.name: Stray Fossa

10169026.bio: Duo making synth- and guitar-driven music inspired by 80s rock, cult movies and technology. Their catalogue includes Juggaar (2018), The Instrumentals (2019) and PRESS START (2023), with a collaboration featuring Jordan Rudess.
10169026.name: McRocklin & Hutch

10293363.bio: Amelia Carey is a young British pop singer-songwriter who emerged around 2018-2019. Her buoyant pop with R&B-leaning electronics deals with love and queer identity, as on the single "Happy Tears", co-written with Jake Roche of Push Baby and AZTX.
10293363.name: Amelia Carey
10293363.note: Origin city not confirmed; UK inferred from Clash coverage

10404097.bio: Tampa-born rapper and singer who broke out with the viral Swamp Bitch and the mixtape Oh the Places You'll Go. Her genre-fluid Alligator Bites Never Heal (2024) won the Grammy for best rap album.
10404097.name: Doechii
10404097.note: No Tidal bio; based on own knowledge, not web-verified

10430738.bio: Free Nationals are a Los Angeles R&B and funk band who long backed Anderson .Paak before releasing their self-titled debut in 2019. The record features guests such as Daniel Caesar and Mac Miller, with a smooth, groove-heavy sound.
10430738.name: Free Nationals

10490331.bio: Band built around Andy Shauf from Regina, Saskatchewan, playing gentle folk- and psych-tinged indie rock. They issued a self-titled debut in 2018 after about ten years of playing together, and a follow-up, 2, in 2025.
10490331.name: Foxwarren

10593.bio: English band led by Mark Hollis who started as synth pop and evolved into the pioneers of art rock and post-rock. Their five studio albums, including The Colour of Spring (1986), Spirit of Eden (1988) and Laughing Stock (1991), grow ever more spacious and experimental.
10593.name: Talk Talk

10616897.bio: Not For Radio is the debut solo project of Maria Zardoya, lead singer of The Marias. Melt (2025) offers hazy mid-tempo grooves with touches of 90s trip hop and Serge Gainsbourg-style bass; Puddles opens the record.
10616897.name: Not For Radio

10636324.bio: Ex:Re is the solo project of Elena Tonra, singer of Daughter. She pairs hushed, introspective songwriting with sparse arrangements, in a similar space to her band. Her self-titled debut came in 2018, followed by a version with the 12 Ensemble in 2021.
10636324.name: Ex:Re

10665.bio: Barbadian pop and R&B superstar Robyn Rihanna Fenty, who rose after 2005 and became the youngest solo artist to reach 13 US number ones. Hits include Umbrella; albums include Anti (2016) and the Wakanda Forever soundtrack contribution (2022).
10665.name: Rihanna

10693662.bio: Chicago trio playing moody yet accessible post-punk, emerging as live music returned after COVID. Releases include 1995 (2022), Bleu (2023) and Bully (2024).
10693662.name: French Police

10711459.bio: Psychedelic rock trio from Lucerne, Switzerland, mixing dark post-apocalyptic atmospheres with ethereal and hypnotic beats. Albums include Wir Sind Da (2023) and Endlich Senden (2026).
10711459.name: Yet No Yokai

10828611.bio: Duo of Laura Les and Dylan Brady, who met through St. Louis' experimental electronic scene and trade tracks online. Their maximalist, genre-smashing hyperpop broke through with 1000 gecs (2019) and continued on 10,000 gecs (2023).
10828611.name: 100 gecs

10859894.bio: Naples collective of Marcello Giannini, Andrea De Fazio and Paolo Petrella, merging psychedelia, groove and improvisation with old southern Italian traditions. Cumbia Mahare, from their 2023 debut, fuses afrobeat and cumbia.
10859894.name: Psyché

10932434.bio: London band formed in 2017 who quickly built a cult following with explosive live shows. Their sound fuses math rock, post-punk, prog and avant-jazz across Schlagenheim (2019), Cavalcade (2021) and Hellfire (2022).
10932434.name: black midi

10979.bio: California dream pop and psychedelic folk duo built around Hope Sandoval and David Roback, from the ashes of Opal. So Tonight That I Might See (1993), with Fade Into You, is their landmark; Seasons of Your Day (2013) followed.
10979.name: Mazzy Star

10984.bio: Notorious Texan band from San Antonio, formed in the early 1980s, known for chaotic, drug-warped psychedelic noise and a shock-value name. Albums such as Locust Abortion Technician (1987) and Electriclarryland (1996, with the hit Pepper) mix hardcore, noise and surreal humor.
10984.name: Butthole Surfers

10995354.bio: Vermont-born indie rock group around songwriter Dana Foote, combining a punky, literate approach with a theatrical style. Albums include I Am The Dog (2023) and Swallow the Knife (2025).
10995354.name: Sir Chloe

11089.bio: Seminal Krautrock duo of drummer Klaus Dinger and guitarist Michael Rother from Düsseldorf. Their driving motorik rhythms and euphoric ambience defined 1970s experimental rock, via Neu! (1972) and Neu! 75 (1975).
11089.name: Neu!

11241.bio: Alternative supergroup formed in Los Angeles by Tool singer Maynard James Keenan and guitarist Billy Howerdel. Their moody, melodic art rock leans on lush textures and theatrical dynamics. Mer de Noms (2000) and Eat the Elephant (2018) are key records.
11241.name: A Perfect Circle

115.bio: One of the best-known jazz pianists and composers, leader of the Dave Brubeck Quartet. Famous for Take Five (written by Paul Desmond) and In Your Own Sweet Way, he popularised odd time signatures in jazz. Time Out (1959) is his landmark album.
115.name: Dave Brubeck

11949.bio: Manchester band that pioneered post-punk with mood and expression over anger, led by Ian Curtis until his death in 1980. Unknown Pleasures (1979) and Closer (1980) and "Love Will Tear Us Apart" are landmarks.
11949.name: Joy Division

11950.bio: New Order formed in Salford in 1980 from the ashes of Joy Division. They fused post-punk with dance and synth pop. Key records include Power, Corruption & Lies (1983), "Blue Monday" and Technique (1989).
11950.name: New Order

12011437.bio: London duo of Sam Fenton and Jezmi Tarik Fehmi, also two-thirds of bar italia, with a lo-fi, hazy slacker and art-rock sound. They self-released Foolish Narratives (2022) and Hardrive Heat Seeking (2023) before signing to Year0001 for Shakedown (2025).
12011437.name: Double Virgo

12034.bio: London trip-hop group centered on Skye Edwards' vocals and Paul and Ross Godfrey's production, mixing funk, blues and fusion. They debuted with the Trigger Hippie EP (1995) and Who Can You Trust? (1996). Recent albums include Blackest Blue (2021).
12034.name: Morcheeba

12125.bio: Swedish new wave revivalists from Helsingborg fronted by Maja Ivarsson, making shimmering synth-washed rock indebted to Blondie and Missing Persons. Living in America (2003) broke through, with later records like Weekend (2013).
12125.name: The Sounds

12173.bio: British duo Henry Binns and Sam Hardaker, spanning trip-hop, downtempo, acid jazz and electronic music. Simple Things (2001) and When It Falls (2004) are highlights.
12173.name: Zero 7

12294454.bio: Philadelphia singer-songwriter best known as the frontwoman of indie rock band Hop Along. Her solo debut Likewise (2020) is an intimate, quirky folk-tinged record with her distinctive quavering voice.
12294454.name: Frances Quinlan

12388120.bio: Frontman of London avant-rock band black midi who went solo in 2024. Born and raised in East London, he released debut The New Sound (2024), an ambitious, theatrical record mixing jazz, Latin music and prog.
12388120.name: Geordie Greep

12451.bio: Michael Balzary, bassist of the Red Hot Chili Peppers, born in Melbourne and raised in Los Angeles, regarded as one of rock's most influential funk-rock bassists. His solo work includes the jazz- and ambient-leaning Honora (2026).
12451.name: Flea

12699.bio: Manchester band led by Morrissey and Johnny Marr, defining 80s British indie guitar pop. Albums include The Smiths (1984), Meat Is Murder (1985) and The Queen Is Dead (1986).
12699.name: The Smiths

13021.bio: Palm Desert desert-rock band often called the Velvet Underground of stoner rock. Blues for the Red Sun (1992), Welcome to Sky Valley (1994) and ...And the Circus Leaves Town (1995) are the key records.
13021.name: Kyuss

13094360.bio: Japanese ambient composer whose early CD-only albums from 1990-91 were later compiled by the Toronto label We Are Busy Bodies as Beach of the Pliocene (2022). The music is quiet and subtle, with affinities to Erik Satie and Satoshi Ashikawa.
13094360.name: Kenichiro Isoda

13492.bio: Los Angeles alt-rock band from the 1990s whose space-rock-tinged records, notably Magnified (1994) and Fantastic Planet (1996), became cult favorites. They reunited in 2014 and returned with The Heart Is a Monster (2015) and Location Lost (2026).
13492.name: Failure

13854437.bio: London-based guitarist, composer and teacher, member of the metal band Monuments from 2011 to 2021, who also releases solo instrumental material. Balance (2019) and Open (2021) are among his singles.
13854437.name: Olly Steele

13972.bio: American industrial-leaning hard rock band founded by Richard Patrick, a former Nine Inch Nails guitarist. Hits like "Hey Man, Nice Shot" (1995) defined mid-90s alternative; recent releases include The Algorithm (2023).
13972.name: Filter

13998.bio: Los Angeles punk-metal band formed in 1985, loud and confrontational, led by Donita Sparks and Suzi Gardner. Known for Bricks Are Heavy (1992) and hit Pretend We're Dead; they reunited in 2014.
13998.name: L7

14123.bio: California band that fused aggressive metal, hip-hop and electronic touches to become a defining act of the early 2000s. Hybrid Theory (2000) and Meteora (2003) were huge; the band returned with From Zero (2024) after Chester Bennington's death.
14123.name: Linkin Park

14143.bio: Walter Becker and Donald Fagen's studio-driven group, famed for defying rock conventions with jazz-inflected, sardonic songwriting and meticulous production. Aja (1977) and Can't Buy a Thrill (1972) are staples.
14143.name: Steely Dan

14347717.bio: Toronto-born, London-based singer, bassist and multi-instrumentalist working in psychedelic pop and alternative R&B. Studied at Berklee, became known for experimental pop on SAYA (2025).
14347717.name: Saya Gray

14375.bio: Jorge Ben Jor is a Brazilian singer-songwriter from Rio de Janeiro, a leading figure of MPB and Tropicália-era samba rock. He has been active since the early 1960s, known for "Mas, Que Nada!" and for albums like África Brasil (1976).
14375.name: Jorge Ben Jor

14630.bio: Folk-rock band from Jamestown, New York, that emerged from the early-80s post-punk underground alongside R.E.M. Led for years by Natalie Merchant, they were known for literate, gentle songs. In Our Tribe (1989) and MTV Unplugged (1993) were their commercial peaks.
14630.name: 10,000 Maniacs

14967.bio: UK band started by Steven Wilson that brought progressive rock back into vogue in the 1990s, filtering it through psychedelia, post-punk and metal. In Absentia (2002) and Fear of a Blank Planet (2007) are key records. They returned with Closure/Continuation in 2022.
14967.name: Porcupine Tree

15122.bio: Irish-English band led by Kevin Shields, who started out as doomy post-punk before defining shoegaze with the walls of guitar noise on Isn't Anything (1988) and Loveless (1991). They returned with m b v in 2013.
15122.name: my bloody valentine

15349.bio: Sacramento alternative metal band that emerged in the 1990s alongside nu-metal but balanced heaviness with atmosphere and beauty. White Pony (2000) is their landmark album, with later records such as Gore (2016) and Ohms (2020). They released private music in 2025.
15349.name: Deftones

15382733.bio: Canadian shoegaze and psych band formed in Ottawa in 2013, later in Toronto. Blends heavy shoegaze and psych into spaced-out dream noise. Paracusis EP (2019), debut album Mirages (2026).
15382733.name: Tijuana Taxi

15426110.bio: New York band blending shoegaze textures, ethereal production and dreamy electronics, echoing early 4AD. Albums include A Color of the Sky (2021) and No Paradise (2024).
15426110.name: Lightning Bug

15429759.bio: Psychedelic project whose debut album Lumin Rain came out in 2025 on Maison Records, later adding vocals with spiritual, world-travel inspired lyrics. Tracks include Mumbo Sugar and The Thief in Marrakesh.
15429759.name: Arc De Soleil

15465368.bio: Indian rapper with a raucous, energetic style informed by Southern and West Coast hip-hop and metal. Debuted with the Kalari EP (2019) and went viral worldwide with "Big Dawgs" (2024).
15465368.name: HanuMankind

15542.bio: Alternative rock band formed in Madison, Wisconsin, fronted by Scottish singer Shirley Manson. They fuse edgy rock with electronic, beat-driven production. Garbage (1995) and Version 2.0 (1998) are the best-known records.
15542.name: Garbage

15544.bio: Toronto duo of drums, bass and vocals, pushing an overdriven mix of punk, hard rock and dance music. Debut You're a Woman, I'm a Machine (2004) made them cult heroes; they returned with The Physical World (2014), Outrage! Is Now (2017) and Is 4 Lovers (2021).
15544.name: Death From Above 1979

1556.bio: Leicester band combining Stone Roses and Primal Scream grooves with big, Oasis-sized swagger and electronics. Albums include Kasabian (2004) and Empire (2006), with the Brit Award-winning Velociraptor! (2011).
1556.name: Kasabian

15589894.bio: Liverpool duo of Hannah Merrick and Craig Whittle, with sparse, atmospheric arrangements that recall Mazzy Star and Portishead alongside fuzzy guitar and minimalist lyrics. Albums include I'm Not Sorry, I Was Just Being Me (2022) and Big Swimmer (2024).
15589894.name: King Hannah

1566.bio: Houston-born pop and R&B superstar who rose with Destiny's Child before a hugely successful solo career. Landmark albums include Lemonade, Renaissance (2022) and the country-leaning Cowboy Carter (2024).
1566.name: Beyoncé

15686643.bio: American singer-songwriter who built an online following with singles in the late 2010s and broke through in 2020. Her moody, confessional pop is influenced by Lorde. Albums include Good Riddance (2023) and The Secret of Us (2024).
15686643.name: Gracie Abrams

15842677.bio: Zurich-based rapper making Swiss German hip hop. His album Easy Going was self-released in 2020, with tracks like 24h Shop and Musig Ohni Kontext.
15842677.name: Lil Bruzy

15998552.bio: The one-off project of David Berman of Silver Jews, releasing a single self-titled album shortly before his death in 2019. Its sad, funny songs like All My Happiness Is Gone made it a late-career highlight.
15998552.name: Purple Mountains

16025988.bio: Crumb are a Brooklyn four-piece formed at Tufts University around 2016, built around Lila Ramani. Their hazy psychedelic sound blends dream pop, jazz and art rock. Key records include Jinx (2019), Ice Melt (2021) and AMAMA (2024).
16025988.name: Crumb

16026508.bio: R&B performer from Zurich, Switzerland who blends funk, jazz and pop into a distinctive sound. The EP Blue Blood (2024) features tracks like Crown and Bow Down, following earlier work such as Blue (2019).
16026508.name: ZZ Amparo

16065992.bio: South London post-punk band pairing taut guitars with Florence Shaw's deadpan spoken-word lyrics. Debut New Long Leg (2021) led to Stumpwork (2022) and Secret Love (2026).
16065992.name: Dry Cleaning

16100815.bio: Natalie Lew's indie project, whose debut LP Diving for a Prize (2025) came out on Luminelle Recordings with producer Andy Park. Dreamy, melancholic guitar pop, preceded by the 2023 single Cellar.
16100815.name: Sea Lemon
16100815.note: Tidal bio describes the sea slug, not the artist; origin unverified.

16127746.bio: Argentine rapper whose recent work includes the EP Universo en Lata (2026), 90s-style rap produced with DJ Koo, following the album Sideral (2024).
16127746.name: Sofía Gabanna

16182414.bio: Melbourne singer-songwriter Olivia Bartley formed Olympia in 2011, inspired by Stina Nordenstam and Neil Young. Indie pop and rock on Self Talk (2016) and Walt Returns (2025).
16182414.name: Olympia

16272768.bio: Los Angeles post-punk band led by Ralph Torrefranca and Sapphire Jewell, with interlocking vocals over fuzzed-out, melodic guitars. They debuted with an EP in 2020, followed by Asymmetry (2021) and All You Got (2024).
16272768.name: Cuffed Up

16288.bio: Manchester project of guitarist Vini Reilly, with an instantly recognisable delicate guitar style on Factory Records. Debut The Return of the Durutti Column (1980) and later works blend ambient, jazz and post-punk.
16288.name: The Durutti Column

16364758.bio: Japanese Heart Software is the solo project of Nat Chippy, making dream pop and chillwave-leaning alternative rock. SOFT (January 2022) is an 8-track album; Desiderium followed in 2026.
16364758.name: Japanese Heart Software

16617727.bio: Bernese-dialect rapper from Switzerland (real name Luc Julian Peyer), mixing grungy trap and party-rap in Swiss German. Releases include the EPs ANTISTYLE (2025) and DiscoTrapper (2026) plus singles like Zistig.
16617727.name: Jule X
16617727.note: No Tidal bio; sources are search snippets.

16622.bio: Boston dream pop trio active 1987-1991, with three albums of reverb-soaked, slow and minimal songs. Influential on slowcore and indie rock, notably through On Fire (1989).
16622.name: Galaxie 500

16699.bio: English ambient trio from Manchester, mixing downtempo post-rock, ambient dub techno and shimmering drone. Best known for the 2011 piece "Weightless"; debut album Under Wires and Searchlights (2003).
16699.name: Marconi Union

16737673.bio: Post-punk trio from Minsk, Belarus, formed in 2017, singing in Russian over cold synths and baritone vocals. Their breakout was Etazhi (2018) and Monument (2020). Belaya Polosa came out in 2024.
16737673.name: Molchat Doma
16737673.note: No Tidal bio; based on general knowledge, not verified by search

16748699.bio: Post-punk and darkwave act from Riga, Latvia, singing in Russian. Releases include the EP Vechnaya osen (2023), a self-titled album (2024) and Chelovecheskiy faktor (2026).
16748699.name: ANAIT

1684.bio: American singer, pianist and civil-rights voice from North Carolina who blended jazz, blues, gospel, classical and folk. Famous for Feeling Good, I Put a Spell on You and Mississippi Goddam; she was active from the late 1950s until the early 2000s.
1684.name: NINA SIMONE

16903707.bio: London band built around singer-songwriter Anouska Sokolow, with a post-punk-tinged indie rock sound drawing on jazz, soul and 90s dream pop. Albums: Honeyglaze (2022) and Real Deal (2024).
16903707.name: Honeyglaze

16917323.bio: Portland, Oregon shoegaze and noise pop band. Their fuzzy, hazy sound is documented on Wallow (2022), Swell (2024) and Alexandra's Band (2025).
16917323.name: Animal Ghosts

17027522.bio: Little-known act on Tidal whose releases include blue dream (2026). Could not find reliable information.
17027522.name: Maono
17027522.note: Could not identify artist; bio based on hints only

17108759.bio: Bristol artist, pioneer of trip hop and former Massive Attack collaborator, with a gritty, claustrophobic style mixing rock, hardcore rap and dancehall. Maxinquaye (1995) is his landmark album, followed by many records including The Golden Lake (2026).
17108759.name: Tricky

17130071.bio: Mo Dotti is a Los Angeles shoegaze quartet named after photographer Tina Modotti. After the EPs Blurring and Guided Imagery (2022), they released debut LP opaque (2024), pairing jangle clarity with clouds of distortion.
17130071.name: Mo Dotti

17208862.bio: Portuguese multi-instrumentalist, singer and producer who has drawn attention from artists like Quincy Jones and Tracy Chapman. Her records include saudade, saudade (2024) and Lifeline (2025).
17208862.name: MARO

17306838.bio: Project of multi-instrumentalist Matthew Doty, sitting between synth pop and shoegaze. Reverb-heavy, ethereal songs evoke M83 and Slowdive. Black Aura My Sun (2020), Every Moment, Everything You Need (2022) and Don't Dare Stop (2023) are the main records.
17306838.name: Deserta

17306868.bio: Sacramento shoegaze duo making moody, noisy pop in the vein of My Bloody Valentine, with blown-out guitars and hazy melodies. Albums include Despondent Transponder (2006) and Occult Radiance (2009).
17306868.name: Fleeting Joys

17359658.bio: Spanish singer and songwriter Lara Fernández Castrelo, born in 2003 in Jerez de la Frontera and based in Madrid. She fuses urban and R&B sounds with Andalusian folk traditions. Her debut is Bodhiria (2024).
17359658.name: Judeline

1736.bio: English singer-songwriter who became a mainstream star at the end of the 1990s with a soft electronic pop sound. Debut No Angel (1999) was one of the UK's best-selling albums, and Thank You went global; later records include Still on My Mind and The Last Summer.
1736.name: Dido

17364.bio: Montreal indie band led by Win Butler and Regine Chassagne, famed for anthemic, orchestral and theatrical live shows. Their debut Funeral (2004) and The Suburbs (2010) are touchstones of 2000s indie rock.
17364.name: Arcade Fire

17449109.bio: Pseudonym Prada is a German-language hip hop act on the iMD-sYNDIKAT label, known for singles like "Beyblade" (2021, with Astro Burger and Anru) and "Passt grad".
17449109.name: Pseudonym Prada
17449109.note: Little information found; origin inferred from German titles

17551.bio: New York band that redefined noise in rock with alternate tunings, dissonance and feedback. Landmarks include Daydream Nation (1988) and Goo (1990) with "Kool Thing" and "Teen Age Riot".
17551.name: Sonic Youth

17582779.bio: Post-punk band, formed in Los Angeles, with angular guitars, dance-punk energy and lo-fi atmospherics that push against power structures. Records include their self-titled debut (2020) and the 8th cumming (2024).
17582779.name: cumgirl8

17665879.bio: London post-punk collective who blend jazz, klezmer, math rock and chamber music into sprawling, dynamic songs. After Isaac Wood left, they reformed as a multi-vocalist band; records include For the First Time (2021), Ants From Up There (2022) and Forever Howlong (2025).
17665879.name: Black Country, New Road

17718.bio: Pond was a 1990s indie band from Portland, Oregon, with Charlie Campbell, Chris Brady and Dave Triebwasser. Their fuzzy psychedelic-leaning rock appears on Pond (1993), The Practice of Joy Before Death (1995) and Rock Collection (1997).
17718.name: Pond
17718.note: Not the Australian Pond despite similar-artist tags (MGMT, Dungen); albums match the 90s band

18134760.bio: Texas-born, New York-based songwriter who built buzz with bedroom pop singles as a teenager, then signed to Sub Pop. Aperture (2023) and Describe (2025) combine ethereal guitar jangle and dreamy vocals.
18134760.name: Hannah Jadagu

18395031.bio: Leeds band merging wiry post-punk with dance-pop, Afrobeat and hip-hop, with a dry sense of humour. Known for The Overload (2022), Where's My Utopia? (2024) and You're Gonna Need a Little Music (2026).
18395031.name: Yard Act

18496884.bio: Asheville, North Carolina band led by Karly Hartzman, mixing alt-country and shoegaze with Southern narratives. Rat Saw God (2023), Bleeds (2025) are key records.
18496884.name: Wednesday
18496884.note: Tidal profile has no bio; identified from the albums Bleeds and Guttering.

18526774.bio: Mundart (Swiss German dialect) rap crew from Wil, St. Gallen, formed around Jan Räbsamen and Gian-Andri Stahl, now a trio. Their humorous, socially critical rap on Planet Erdbeertörtli (2021) and Moralpanik (2023) is energetic and live-driven.
18526774.name: Projekt ET

18581469.bio: Spanish noise-pop band inspired by Joanna Gruesome, Veronica Falls and riot grrrl acts like Bikini Kill. Their scrappy debut Va totalmente en serio... arrived in 2020, followed by the denser Me están apuntando con un arma in 2023 and Señales Brutales in 2026.
18581469.name: Aiko el grupo

18594582.bio: Psychedelic folk rock band from Tel Aviv, inspired by the Turkish psychedelic wave of the 60s and 70s. They mix Anatolian melodies, psych guitars and disco rhythms on Aylar (2025).
18594582.name: Şatellites

18786.bio: Montreal indie rock project of Elizabeth Powell, with spiky, raucous early records and a more experimental later phase questioning social expectations. Albums include Applause Cheer Boo Hiss (2006) and Indistinct Conversations (2020).
18786.name: Land Of Talk

18793679.bio: Irish band from Galway led by Julie Dawson, offering fuzzy, shimmering alt rock with 80s and 90s leanings. Debut EP Waves (2021), then Madra (2024) and Altar (2025).
18793679.name: NewDad

19151.bio: Formed in Duluth, Minnesota in 1993, Low became the defining slowcore band: spare, hushed and hypnotic. Later work grew more experimental, notably Double Negative (2018) and HEY WHAT (2021).
19151.name: Low

19232.bio: Otis Jackson Jr., prolific California producer, DJ and rapper active since the early 1990s under aliases such as Quasimoto and Beat Konducta. Madvillainy (with MF Doom) and Bandana (with Freddie Gibbs) stand out.
19232.name: Madlib

1936.bio: First of the San Francisco psychedelic groups of the 1960s to reach national recognition. Hits such as White Rabbit and Somebody to Love came from Surrealistic Pillow (1967), with Grace Slick on vocals. Their sound shaped the West Coast acid rock era.
1936.name: Jefferson Airplane

19368.bio: Aberdeen, Washington trio fronted by Kurt Cobain whose second album Nevermind (1991) pushed alternative rock into the mainstream. Key records also include Bleach (1989) and In Utero (1993).
19368.name: Nirvana

19379.bio: Wolfmother are an Australian rock revival band from Sydney, with thick fuzz guitars and primal psychedelia. Their self-titled debut (2005) produced "Woman" and "Joker and the Thief".
19379.name: Wolfmother

19450.bio: Hawaiian singer-songwriter and former pro surfer known for mellow, acoustic beach-folk. Breakthrough Brushfire Fairytales (2001) led to hits like Banana Pancakes and Better Together on In Between Dreams (2005).
19450.name: Jack Johnson

19469673.bio: Project of Alicia Bognanno, a Minnesota-born sound engineer based in Nashville, making punk-leaning, grungy power-pop with raw confessional lyrics. Debut Feels Like (2015) led to Losing (2017), SUGEREGG (2020) and Lucky for You (2023).
19469673.name: Bully

19488958.bio: Go Kurosawa is a Japanese multi-instrumentalist and producer, co-founder of Guruguru Brain and drummer-vocalist of Kikagaku Moyo. His first solo album soft shakes (2025) was made alone, drifting between psych, folk strums, funk and lounge textures.
19488958.name: Go Kurosawa

19632300.bio: Heavy metal band from Lomé, Togo, widely described as the country's first, blending groove and thrash metal with Ewe folk music and African percussion. Albums include Fighting Spirits Within (2019) and Dzikkuh (2024).
19632300.name: Arka'n Asrafokor

19849400.bio: Costa Rican band from San José who blend shoegaze, post-rock, dream pop and post-hardcore. Their debut album Nuestras Manos Son Incendios (2024) swings between furious catharsis and ambient calm, and Un destello de luz followed in 2026.
19849400.name: Adiós Cometa

19912429.bio: Leonora Post Punk is a Mexican rock and indie act whose 2020 EP Eternos includes the tracks "Eternos" and "Insomnio", sung in Spanish. Melancholic post-punk with sweet vocals and driving guitars.
19912429.name: Leonora Post Punk

2004.bio: Danish duo of Sune Rose Wagner and Sharin Foo, combining the Jesus and Mary Chain's noise with 1950s rock and roll and 1960s girl-group melody. Their debut The Chain Gang of Love (2003) set the style; PE'AHI II arrived in 2025.
2004.name: The Raveonettes

20401509.bio: Wellington, New Zealand rapper and musician Kalem Leo Tarrant, born 2000. Works across dark trap, phonk, trap metal and experimental hip hop; recent album EXISTENTIAL CRISIS (2026).
20401509.name: SXMPRA

20448658.bio: DannyLux is Daniel Balderrama, a singer, songwriter and guitarist from Palm Springs, California, combining corrido and sad sierreño with classic and alternative rock. He broke through in 2020 on Eslabon Armado's Jugaste y Sufrí and released LEYENDA in 2025.
20448658.name: DannyLux

205.bio: Canadian-born singer-songwriter and guitarist with a career spanning from acoustic folk and country rock to raw, feedback-heavy electric work with Crazy Horse. Landmarks include Harvest (1972), After the Gold Rush (1970) and Rust Never Sleeps (1979).
205.name: Neil Young

20931.bio: Sonic Youth co-founder and guitarist, active in experimental and noise rock solo work since Psychic Hearts (1995). Later records include Rock n Roll Consciousness and Flow Critical Lucidity (2024).
20931.name: Thurston Moore

20951997.bio: Austin, Texas dream pop project of Julian Berdegue, writing and performing everything himself. Releases include Eventide (2023) and Lifelines (2025), described as lucid and weightless.
20951997.name: EVNTYD

21159820.bio: London trio of three singer-songwriters whose woozy, murky indie rock drifts between post-punk, slowcore and lo-fi pop. They emerged with Tracey Denim (2023) and signed to Matador, following up with The Twits (2023) and Some Like It Hot (2025).
21159820.name: bar italia

21445.bio: Husband-and-wife duo Alaina Moore and Patrick Riley, who met at University of Colorado in 2008 and came out of Denver's DIY scene. Their breezy pop includes Swimmer (2020), Pollen (2023) and Face Down in the Garden (2025).
21445.name: Tennis

21556526.bio: Vacíos Cuerpos is a Mexican post-punk and coldwave project from Oaxaca, formed in 2019, using drum machines, dark melodies and disillusioned lyrics. Records include Doble Mente EP (2020), Laberinto (2022) and La Cruz de Mi Conciencia (2025).
21556526.name: Vacíos Cuerpos

21985064.bio: Spirit of the Beehive are a Philadelphia band that dart between styles, from dream pop to noise and psych. Key records include Hypnic Jerks (2018), Entertainment, Death (2021) and You'll Have to Lose Something (2024).
21985064.name: SPIRIT OF THE BEEHIVE

22221428.bio: Philadelphia band of Jack Chaffer, Cassidy Rose Hammond and Dylan Vaisey, mixing shoegaze, noise pop, neo-psychedelia and drum and bass textures. The 2022 compilation 2020initialsequence2022 collects their early demos and EPs.
22221428.name: Full Body 2

22568466.bio: Stage name of Florida musician Nick Quan, blending shoegaze, lo-fi, noise and electronic bedroom pop. Albums include Kenopsia (2022), Stepdream (2023) and Warbrained (2025), and he has toured with Jane Remover and Slowdive.
22568466.name: quannnic

22719534.bio: Five-piece Brooklyn band whose members lived together in a maze-like house while writing their album Channels (2024). Details beyond the Tidal text are limited.
22719534.name: Punchlove

22938648.bio: Sakanaction are a Japanese band from Sapporo, led by Ichiro Yamaguchi, who shift between rock and electronic dance styles. Key records include Sakanaction (2013) and Kikuuiki (2014).
22938648.name: Sakanaction

23067787.bio: San Francisco Bay Area rapper and singer-songwriter born in 2001, who found an audience with the TikTok-friendly single mr. sunshine from age tape 8 (2022). His melodic, upbeat hip hop and pop-leaning cuts continue on the album FLASH (2026).
23067787.name: Arden Jones
23067787.note: Tidal bio is a one-liner, not used; bio from web search.

23409727.bio: London producer and singer with a wry, stream-of-consciousness style and sample-heavy sound rooted in house, UK garage and drum'n'bass. Albums include Heaven Knows (2023) and Fancy That (2025).
23409727.name: PinkPantheress

23927301.bio: Masked Melbourne trio blending Western psychedelia with Indian and Middle Eastern melodic influences, in a similar space to Khruangbin. Their EPs Mirage (2022) and Mahal (2023) and album Mahal built a sizable following.
23927301.name: Glass Beams

24178234.bio: Paris, Texas appears here under the Tidal bio of a Madison, Wisconsin emo band formed in 1997, but the albums They Left Me With a Gun (2025) suggest a different, LA-based hip hop duo of the same name.
24178234.name: Paris Texas
24178234.note: Tidal profile may be a different artist with the same name; the albums fit the LA duo Paris Texas

24449964.bio: Indie pop project of Constantin Kopp from Helmstedt, Germany. Best known for the album 999 (2022) and the track gardenfulloflight.
24449964.name: Dolphin Love
24449964.note: Tidal bio is just 'peace and love'; details from web sources.

24516191.bio: Pittsburgh guitar band making noisy, jangly indie rock and shoegaze-adjacent songs. Records include Hayday (2021), Girl with Fish (2023) and bitknot (2026).
24516191.name: feeble little horse

24905.bio: Los Angeles singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who has hopped between lo-fi folk, funk, hip hop collage and orchestral pop. Odelay (1996) made him an alternative icon, with Sea Change (2002) and Morning Phase (2014) among later landmarks.
24905.name: Beck

24912.bio: Polly Jean Harvey, English singer-songwriter from Dorset who emerged in the early 1990s with raw alt-rock and has continually reinvented herself. Key records include Dry (1992), To Bring You My Love (1995), Let England Shake (2011) and I Inside the Old Year Dying (2023).
24912.name: PJ Harvey

24959.bio: Progressive rock band formed in 2001 by Omar Rodriguez-Lopez and Cedric Bixler-Zavala from At the Drive-In. Their sound mixes hardcore intensity, prog, psychedelia and avant-jazz. De-Loused in the Comatorium (2003) and Frances the Mute (2005) stand out.
24959.name: The Mars Volta

25399116.bio: Isle of Wight duo of Rhian Teasdale and Hester Chambers, bringing playful, candid humour to post-punk. Chaise Longue (2021) made them viral stars; albums are Wet Leg (2022) and moisturizer (2025).
25399116.name: Wet Leg

27196553.bio: English singer-songwriter and guitarist Madeleine Haenlein, born in London, who debuted in 2021 with the single Slugeye. Her darker, grungy indie-rock, partly inspired by Nick Cave, appears on the EPs Slugeye (2022) and Head of the Love Club (2023), and on debut album Squish (2026).
27196553.name: Gretel Hänlyn

27309.bio: Portland band led by Colin Meloy, writing theatrical, literate folk-influenced pop with 60s British folk and 80s college rock roots. Albums include Picaresque (2005), The Crane Wife (2006) and As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again (2024).
27309.name: The Decemberists

27439.bio: Glasgow indie rock band that arrived in the early-2000s rock revival with sharp, danceable guitar hooks. Their self-titled 2004 debut brought Take Me Out and Do You Want To; later albums include Always Ascending (2018) and The Human Fear (2025).
27439.name: Franz Ferdinand

27441.bio: Bristol trio, among the first to popularise trip hop, with Beth Gibbons's yearning vocals over slow, cinematic beats. Dummy (1994) and Third (2008) are key albums.
27441.name: Portishead

27446.bio: Garage rock duo of Alison Mosshart and Jamie Hince, formed in London from American-British collaboration. They strip rock down to essentials, from Keep on Your Mean Side (2003) to God Games (2023).
27446.name: The Kills

27488.bio: New York art punk trio of Karen O, Nick Zinner and Brian Chase. Their 2001 EP kicked off a garage rock revival hit; Fever to Tell (2003), It's Blitz! (2009) and Cool It Down (2022) show evolution.
27488.name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs

27911777.bio: Stage name of Peruvian musician Lenin Tamayo Pinares, creator of what he calls Quechua pop, singing in Quechua over art-pop and electronic arrangements. Releases include the singles Imaynata? (2022) and Intiraymi (2022), and the albums AMARU I and II.
27911777.name: L E N I N

28101.bio: Reading shoegaze band that began as a drony space rock act playing with Spacemen 3 and then moved toward dance-influenced guitar pop. Their early 90s peak includes the album Whirlpool (1991); they reformed in the late 2010s and released The Oregon Trail (2019).
28101.name: Chapterhouse

28928664.bio: Mary in the junkyard are a British indie rock trio with a DIY ethos, who broke through in 2023 with the jangly debut single "Tuesday". Role Model Hermit followed in 2026.
28928664.name: mary in the junkyard

29037.bio: New York band that revived hooky, stylish garage rock with Is This It (2001), inspired by the Velvet Underground and Ramones. Later records include Room on Fire, First Impressions of Earth and The New Abnormal (2020).
29037.name: The Strokes

29432158.bio: Chilean artist, songwriter and producer Fran Straube, praised for dark, alchemical avant-pop. Records include Mango Negro (2020), Venus & Blue (2023) and Espero podamos ver un ovni juntxs (2026).
29432158.name: Rubio

29517954.bio: Swiss artist making bass-heavy electronic pop and experimental music with symbolic lyrics. Releases include Crybaby (2023), the Pastelfuneral collaboration Thelxiepeia (2024), and Bloodmoss and Life's Too Short Not to Attempt to Fly (2025).
29517954.name: Lisheva

29575.bio: Peruvian singer-songwriter with a multi-decade career who found his greatest success as a songwriter for Latin pop stars. Solo albums A Tiempo (2002) and Resucitar (2004) were produced by Emilio Estefan Jr.; recent work includes Mandarina (2021).
29575.name: Gian Marco

29893.bio: Dire Straits were an English rock band formed in London in 1977 by Mark Knopfler. Their stripped-down, guitar-led roots rock was unlike punk. Key records include the self-titled debut (1978), Making Movies (1980) and Brothers in Arms (1985).
29893.name: Dire Straits

29902.bio: Heavy rock band from Palm Desert, California, led by Josh Homme, emerging from the 1990s stoner scene. Rated R (2000) took them mainstream; later albums include ...Like Clockwork (2013), Villains (2017) and In Times New Roman... (2023).
29902.name: Queens Of The Stone Age

30058791.bio: The Smile is a UK trio of Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood of Radiohead with drummer Tom Skinner of Sons of Kemet. They debuted with A Light for Attracting Attention (2022), followed by Wall of Eyes and Cutouts (2024).
30058791.name: The Smile

30157.bio: Los Angeles power-pop and alternative rock band that rose in the mid-90s with the Blue Album (1994) and Pinkerton (1996). Hits like Say It Ain't So and Island in the Sun come from a long, prolific career, including the SZNZ series (2022).
30157.name: Weezer

30283.bio: James Lavelle's project since 1992, cofounder of Mo' Wax, with a rotating cast of collaborators. Psyence Fiction (1998) is the landmark of their trip-hop and electronic sound; recent: Rōnin I and II.
30283.name: UNKLE

30573924.bio: Minneapolis dream pop band moving from washed-out shoegaze guitars to full-band explosions, growing denser from home recordings. Their 2026 release is swallowtail.
30573924.name: She's Green

30814.bio: English band from St Albans, one of the finest mid-1960s groups, with Colin Blunstone's breathy vocals and Rod Argent's keys. Odessey and Oracle (1968) and the hit Time of the Season are classics; they reunited in 2000s and issued Different Game (2023).
30814.name: The Zombies

31816.bio: British guitar band from Great Yarmouth active in the 1990s, pairing swirling distorted guitars with airy vocals. Albums like Chrome (1993), Happy Days (1995) and Adam and Eve (1997) placed them among the more melodic shoegaze-adjacent alt-rock acts.
31816.name: Catherine Wheel

32191798.bio: Blondshell is the project of Sabrina Teitelbaum, a Los Angeles singer-songwriter blending confessional lyrics with steely alt-rock. She broke out in 2022 with Olympus, then released her self-titled debut in 2023 and Another Picture in 2025.
32191798.name: Blondshell

32230107.bio: Yuli de Souza is a Mexican singer-songwriter who pays homage to 90s and 2000s sounds, fusing pop, trap and rap. Her songs include "Quiero Ser" (2023).
32230107.name: Yuli de Souza

32251676.bio: Singer-songwriter whose gruff, angst-ridden storytelling mixes alternative country-rock, pop-rap and anthemic pop. Debuted in 2022 with the viral song THE ONLY TIME IT RAINS IN HOLLYWOOD; recent record TAHOE (2026).
32251676.name: Red Leather

32313.bio: Brooklyn duo Busy Gangnes and Melissa Livaudais who moved from improvisational drones to experimental, danceable pop. Albums include Dance Mother (2009), produced by Dave Sitek, and Destroyer (2015).
32313.name: Telepathe

32458.bio: Austin indie rock band that started as brash post-punkers in the mid-90s and became known for inventive, concise songwriting. Gimme Fiction (2005), Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga (2007) and Lucifer on the Sofa (2022) stand out.
32458.name: Spoon

32720578.bio: Alternative metal band from Moscow, blending shoegaze, grunge and metal with a nostalgic MTV-era feel. Known for the 2022 singles Cry Wolf and Closer.
32720578.name: Sundazer

32954.bio: Australian singer-songwriter with a distinctive voice who writes hits for herself and others. Known for Chandelier and albums such as 1000 Forms of Fear (2014) and This Is Acting (2016).
32954.name: Sia

33043.bio: Rotating, jam-style collective founded by Josh Homme and friends, rooted in desert generator parties and the Queens of the Stone Age circle. Each Desert Sessions volume pairs different guests, with Vols. 11 and 12 arriving in 2019.
33043.name: Desert Sessions

33307428.bio: Chilean post-rock sextet from Santiago whose long-form songs mix post-punk, noise rock and prog with saxophone and jazzy touches. Records are the 80-minute La Brea (2025) and Morir Saltando (2026).
33307428.name: Hesse Kassel

34477.bio: Seattle band that carved a place for heavy metal in alternative rock, drawing on sludgy 70s riffs. Badmotorfinger (1991) and Superunknown (1994, with Black Hole Sun) are landmarks; Chris Cornell died in 2017.
34477.name: Soundgarden

34541.bio: Scottish trio from Grangemouth, central to the 4AD sound, with Elizabeth Fraser's wordless, otherworldly vocals over shimmering guitars. Treasure (1984), Heaven or Las Vegas (1990) and Blue Bell Knoll are defining albums of dream pop.
34541.name: Cocteau Twins

3500082.bio: Pioneering American soul singer who moved from gospel to pop in the 1950s and helped invent the genre. Hits include A Change Is Gonna Come and Wonderful World; he died in 1964.
3500082.name: Sam Cooke

3501074.bio: Evolving vehicle of Anton Newcombe, a prolific psych-rock band since the mid-90s from San Francisco. Records include Their Satanic Majesties' Second Request (1996), Methodrone (1995) and Fire Doesn't Grow on Trees (2022).
3501074.name: The Brian Jonestown Massacre

3501428.bio: Singer-songwriter from Portland, Oregon (raised in Texas), known for intimate, melodically rich songs and hushed, double-tracked vocals. He began in the band Heatmiser; Either/Or (1997) and XO (1998) made him a star after the Oscar-nominated Miss Misery. He died in 2003.
3501428.name: Elliott Smith

3501486.bio: Courtney Love's Los Angeles band, noisy and abrasive in the early days and polished by the late 90s. Pretty on the Inside (1991), Live Through This (1994) and Celebrity Skin (1998) are its key records.
3501486.name: Hole

3503611.bio: Seattle emo band whose short-lived original run included the classic Diary (1994) and LP2 (1995). They reunited in the 1990s and 2000s with albums like How It Feels to Be Something On and The Rising Tide (2000).
3503611.name: Sunny Day Real Estate

3504370.bio: Duo of Ben Goldwasser and Andrew VanWyngarden, formed at Wesleyan in 2002. Oracular Spectacular (2007), with Kids and Electric Feel, was a hit; later work like Loss of Life (2024) leans into art-rock psychedelia.
3504370.name: MGMT

3505228.bio: Reading shoegaze band whose swirling guitars grew into folk, dub and electronic ideas. Just for a Day (1991) and Souvlaki (1993) are classics; after reuniting they made Slowdive (2017) and everything is alive (2023).
3505228.name: Slowdive

3516413.bio: Chilean folk-rock pioneers from Vina del Mar, formed in the 1960s, who fused Andean folk instruments with progressive and psychedelic rock. Landmark records include Alturas de Machu Picchu (1981), and they have long been a pillar of Latin American rock.
3516413.name: Los Jaivas

3518222.bio: Simon Green's electronic project, debuting with the sample-based downtempo album Animal Magic in 2000. His music is organic and layered, suited to both chilling out and dancing. Black Sands (2010) and Migration (2017) are standout records.
3518222.name: Bonobo

3518502.bio: Aim is Andy Turner, a British producer who started out as a rap DJ in 1989 and signed to Manchester's Grand Central label. His cinematic trip-hop and downtempo draws on hip hop and jazz. Key records include Cold Water Music (1999) and Hinterland.
3518502.name: AIM

3518535.bio: British trip-hop group from Hartlepool, best known for Becoming X (1996) and its hit 6 Underground. They shifted toward rock and electronica on Splinter (1999) and Bloodsport (2002) and returned with Squaring the Circle (2021).
3518535.name: Sneaker Pimps

3519311.bio: Beach House is a Baltimore dream pop duo of Victoria Legrand and Alex Scally. Formed in 2004, they moved from lo-fi beginnings on their 2006 debut to a polished, expansive sound. Key records include Teen Dream (2010), Bloom (2012), 7 (2018) and Once Twice Melody (2022).
3519311.name: Beach House

3519571.bio: Swedish quartet from Gothenburg fronted by Yukimi Nagano, blending downtempo electronic pop with R&B, hip-hop and left-field dance. Albums include Machine Dreams (2009), Nabuma Rubberband (2014) and Slugs of Love (2023).
3519571.name: Little Dragon

3519747.bio: Apparat is the project of German producer Sascha Ring. He began with glitchy IDM and techno in the early 2000s before moving toward orchestrated, emotive electronic pop. Key records include Walls (2007), The Devil's Walk (2011) and the Berlin-based Soundtracks work.
3519747.name: APPARAT

3520508.bio: Experimental band that grew from a group of childhood friends in Baltimore and became a defining name in indie experimental rock. Known for the glossy, loop-driven Merriweather Post Pavilion (2009) and hits like "My Girls".
3520508.name: Animal Collective

3520710.bio: Sheffield indie rock band that broke through in 2005-06 on internet buzz with Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not. Led by Alex Turner, they evolved from jittery guitar rock to desert rock (AM, 2013) and lounge-style concept records like Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino (2018) and The Car (2022).
3520710.name: Arctic Monkeys

3520717.bio: Kieran Hebden, British producer who blends organic sounds with electronic production for a warm, experimental style loved by indie and dance fans. Key records include Rounds (2003), There Is Love in You (2010) and Three (2024).
3520717.name: Four Tet

3520731.bio: Dev Hynes' folk-leaning project launched after the dissolution of Test Icicles in 2006. Falling Off the Lavender Bridge (2008) showed his pop melodies and country-folk leanings, followed by Life Is Sweet! Nice to Meet You (2010). Hynes later became known as Blood Orange.
3520731.name: Lightspeed Champion

3520832.bio: Swedish singer-songwriter of Argentine parentage, known for hushed nylon-string guitar folk and covers like Heartbeats. Veneer (2003) and In Our Nature (2007) made his name, with later records including Local Valley and a 2026 album.
3520832.name: José González

3524587.bio: Little-known act on Tidal, apparently Hungarian-language, whose 2025 releases include Rossz döntések, jó emlékek, Szegedi Retek and VIBIN'. No reliable profile found.
3524587.name: Swain
3524587.note: Could not identify artist; origin inferred from Hungarian album titles

3529073.bio: English electronic producer and composer, a collaborator of Brian Eno and Coldplay, who blends ambient textures with techno propulsion. Notable albums are Immunity (2013), Singularity (2018) and Music for Psychedelic Therapy (2021).
3529073.name: Jon Hopkins

3531724.bio: Steven Ellison, Los Angeles producer and Brainfeeder label founder, blending hip hop, experimental electronic music and avant-garde jazz. Emerging in 2006 in the Dilla and Madlib mold, he made Cosmogramma (2010) and You're Dead! (2014), and later scored film work.
3531724.name: Flying Lotus

3532352.bio: Bosnian-German DJ, producer and Diynamic label co-founder in Hamburg, with melodic, emotional deep house, melodic techno and indie dance. Known for Nobody Is Not Loved and remixes.
3532352.name: Solomun

3533548.bio: London alternative group built around Toni Halliday and Dean Garcia, mixing towering guitar noise with dance beats, goth gloom and airy melodies. They were active from 1990 to 2005, with Doppelgänger (1992) their best-known album.
3533548.name: Curve

3533999.bio: Logic is a Maryland rapper, singer and producer who rose through mixtapes. His lyrical, mainstream-friendly hip hop includes Under Pressure (2014), Everybody (2017) and the hit "1-800-273-8255".
3533999.name: Logic

3537180.bio: San Francisco duo of Meric Long and drummer Logan Kroeber, blending breezy melodies with kinetic experimental drumming and nimble guitar. Visiter (2008) was their breakthrough, with later records including Grizzly Peak (2021) and Kablooey (2025).
3537180.name: The Dodos

3537908.bio: New York group formed in the early 1990s around the Pace twins and Kazu Makino, moving from noisy no wave toward dark, romantic, cinematic dream pop. Records like Misery Is a Butterfly (2004), 23 (2007) and Sit Down for Dinner (2023) show their ever-evolving sound; The Shadow of the Guest followed in 2025.
3537908.name: Blonde Redhead

3539944.bio: Metronomy is the project of Joseph Mount from Devon, England, mixing electronic pop and indie rock with witty melodies. Key records include Nights Out (2008), The English Riviera (2011) and Love Letters (2014).
3539944.name: Metronomy

3539965.bio: Philadelphia band around Adam Granduciel, pairing grand-scale guitars with Dylan and Springsteen-esque lyricism. Albums include Slave Ambient (2011), Lost in the Dream (2014) and I Don't Live Here Anymore (2021).
3539965.name: The War On Drugs

3541669.bio: Montreal singer, pianist and film composer making explorative chamber pop, solo and with his band of the same name. To Build a Home (with the Cinematic Orchestra) is his best known song. Records include Close to Paradise (2009) and Wave (2019).
3541669.name: Patrick Watson

3544256.bio: Radiohead frontman whose solo work explores electronics and experimental song. Releases include The Eraser (2006), ANIMA (2019) and Tall Tales (2025).
3544256.name: Thom Yorke

3544875.bio: London-based folk-pop band who rose with Peaceful, the World Lays Me Down (2008) and the hit 5 Years Time; Laura Marling started in the lineup. Later albums include The First Days of Spring (2009) and Heart of Nowhere (2013).
3544875.name: Noah And The Whale

3546968.bio: Michigan band formed in the early 2010s, mixing emo, post-hardcore, shoegaze and heavy indie rock. They broke out with Youth (2013) and have continued through As You Please (2017) and Calling the Dogs (2023).
3546968.name: CITIZEN

3547534.bio: London trio fronted by Elena Tonra, blending moody folk, hushed electronics and pop. Albums include If You Leave (2013), Not to Disappear (2016) and Stereo Mind Game (2023).
3547534.name: Daughter

3551890.bio: Danish indie band formed in 2012 by friends from Silkeborg who moved to Copenhagen, with jangly, hazy noise pop. Albums include Virgin Suicide (2015) and Forever Trouble (2017).
3551890.name: Virgin Suicide

3553421.bio: Scottish band from East Kilbride formed by brothers Jim and William Reid, mixing Velvet Underground-style noise and feedback with pop melodies. Psychocandy (1985) was hugely influential; they later released Damage and Joy (2017) and Glasgow Eyes (2024).
3553421.name: The Jesus and Mary Chain

3555856.bio: Indie collective led by Zach Condon from Santa Fe, New Mexico, debuting in 2006 with Gulag Orkestar. Their sound mixes Balkan brass, European folk and chamber pop, later adding electronics. Also notable are The Flying Club Cup (2007) and Hadsel (2023).
3555856.name: Beirut

3556217.bio: Canadian twin sisters from Calgary who began with folk-punk-tinged harmonies and moved into polished indie pop. Albums include The Con (2007), Heartthrob (2013) and Crybaby (2022).
3556217.name: Tegan and Sara

3560068.bio: Rock supergroup of Jack White and Brendan Benson that began as a side project in the White Stripes era. Albums include Broken Boy Soldiers (2006), Consolers of the Lonely (2008) and Help Us Stranger (2019).
3560068.name: The Raconteurs

3561926.bio: Canadian indie rock band from Montreal, formed by Spencer Krug and Dan Boeckner, building catchy songs on 1980s synth new wave. Apologies to the Queen Mary (2005) led to Cry Cry Cry (2017) and Thin Mind (2020).
3561926.name: Wolf Parade

3565237.bio: Brooklyn band blending post-punk, electronics, soul and funk. Return to Cookie Mountain (2006) and Dear Science (2008) are acclaimed; later albums include Nine Types of Light and Seeds (2014).
3565237.name: TV On The Radio

3565241.bio: San Francisco band, later Los Angeles, mixing post-punk and shoegaze with lush, sometimes poppy melodies. Albums include Hideout (2006), Fission (2007), and recent returns such as Field (2023).
3565241.name: Film School

3565264.bio: Mark Kozelek's San Francisco band, known for emotionally intense, slow and spare songs. Albums such as Down Colorful Hill, Ocean Beach (1995) and Old Ramon (2001) set the template for slowcore.
3565264.name: Red House Painters

3565988.bio: London shoegaze and dream pop band led by Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson on 4AD. Spooky (1992) and Split are early classics, and Lovelife (1996) brought Britpop-era hits; they reformed in 2015.
3565988.name: Lush

3566020.bio: The Libertines are an English band from London, led by Carl Barât and Pete Doherty. Their brash, melodic garage rock revived British traditions. Key records include Up the Bracket (2002) and The Libertines (2004).
3566020.name: The Libertines

3566081.bio: Singer-songwriter born in Texas and raised partly in Venezuela, a central figure of the 2000s freak folk scene with a quivering, warm voice. Notable albums include Cripple Crow (2005), Rejoicing in the Hands and Ma (2019).
3566081.name: Devendra Banhart

3566193.bio: Manhattan drone-rock duo of Lawrence Chandler and Martha Schwendener, later with a drummer, combining shoegaze, ambient and trip-hop textures with slow-motion guitars. Key albums are Beat (1996), Vertigo (1997) and Lushlife (2000).
3566193.name: Bowery Electric

3566263.bio: Swedish indie pop band from Lund, built around Johan Duncanson and Martin Larsson, with hazy synths and dreamy guitars. Albums include Lesser Matters (2003), Pet Grief (2006), Clinging to a Scheme (2010) and Running Out of Love (2016).
3566263.name: The Radio Dept.
3566263.note: No Tidal bio; classification from background knowledge

3566316.bio: Atlanta band led by Bradford Cox, shifting between experimental noise and wistful chiming pop since the mid-2000s. Key records include Halcyon Digest (2010) and Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared? (2019).
3566316.name: Deerhunter

3566323.bio: Vampire Weekend is a New York indie rock band formed at Columbia University, mixing Afropop, ska, hip hop and 80s pop. Key records include Vampire Weekend (2008), Modern Vampires of the City (2013) and Father of the Bride (2019).
3566323.name: Vampire Weekend

3571150.bio: Brooklyn indie rock band formed in 2003 by Brad Hargett and JB Townsend, with reverb-soaked, lo-fi sound reminiscent of Velvet Underground and C86. Their first singles appeared in 2004, and Alight of Night (2008) was their debut album. In Love With Oblivion (2011) followed.
3571150.name: Crystal Stilts

3571151.bio: Vivian Girls were a Brooklyn trio from the late-2000s lo-fi indie scene, mixing 60s girl-group melodies with noisy fuzz. They released Vivian Girls (2008) and Everything Goes Wrong (2009), and reformed in 2019 with Memory.
3571151.name: Vivian Girls

3571160.bio: New York noise-pop group led by Kip Berman, balancing fragile melodies with walls of fuzz in the Slumberland tradition. Albums include their 2009 debut, Belong (2011) and Days of Abandon (2014), with The Echo of Pleasure in 2017.
3571160.name: The Pains Of Being Pure At Heart

3571162.bio: Los Angeles noise and industrial rock band built around dense guitars, synths and Jake Duzsik's atmospheric vocals. Records include Get Color (2007), Death Magic (2015) and Conflict DLC (2025).
3571162.name: HEALTH

3574977.bio: Helium was a 1990s Boston indie band led by guitarist Mary Timony, known for experimental guitar and by turns tough and vulnerable vocals. Key records include The Dirt of Luck (1995) and The Magic City (1997). They reunited briefly for Ends with And (2017).
3574977.name: Helium

3574987.bio: Olympia, Washington DIY punk trio whose noisy, tumultuous music grew in the shadow of grunge. Albums include Repetition (1996) and Leaves Turn Inside You (2001).
3574987.name: Unwound

3575091.bio: Indie rock band of former Pavement leader Stephen Malkmus, formed in Portland around 2000. Albums include Mirror Traffic (2011), Wig Out at Jagbags (2014) and Sparkle Hard (2018), mixing slacker lyrics with loose guitar jamming.
3575091.name: Stephen Malkmus & The Jicks
3575091.note: Tidal bio missing; bio from general knowledge and hints

3578350.bio: Brooklyn band that rose from high-school rockers to buzzy indie names with nervy, jittery post-punk. Albums include Projector (2021), 3D Country (2023) and Getting Killed (2025).
3578350.name: Geese

3579242.bio: London band, among the first wave of British punk, releasing the first UK punk single (New Rose, 1976). Later they added goth and psychedelic touches on Machine Gun Etiquette (1979) and Phantasmagoria (1985); they have continued into the 2020s.
3579242.name: The Damned

3580102.bio: Oxford band, one of the foundational first-wave shoegaze groups, whose early records Nowhere (1990) and Going Blank Again (1992) defined the genre before they split in 1996. They reunited in 2014 and released Weather Diaries (2017), This Is Not a Safe Place (2019) and Interplay (2024).
3580102.name: Ride

3584091.bio: Tuareg collective from the Malian Sahara, pioneers of tishoumaren desert blues with percussive, guitar-centered songs. Albums include The Radio Tisdas Sessions (2001), Aman Iman (2007) and Hoggar (2026).
3584091.name: Tinariwen

3586448.bio: Grizzly Bear began as Ed Droste's home recording project in Brooklyn and became an acclaimed indie rock group blending psych, folk, classical and jazz. Key records include Veckatimest (2009), Shields (2012) and Painted Ruins (2017).
3586448.name: Grizzly Bear

3589987.bio: English indie pop band blending jangly Smiths-like guitars with Cocteau Twins-style dream pop, with Harriet Wheeler's voice. Reading, Writing and Arithmetic (1990) and Blind (1992) were acclaimed, followed by Static & Silence (1997).
3589987.name: The Sundays

3603101.bio: Drop Nineteens were a Boston shoegaze band active 1991-1995 and reunited from 2013. Their debut Delaware (1992) and National Coma (1993) are noted American shoegaze records. A new album, Hard Light, followed in 2023.
3603101.name: Drop Nineteens

3604053.bio: San Francisco hardcore punk band led by Jello Biafra, famous for sharp political satire. Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables (1980) and songs like "California Uber Alles" made them a landmark of American punk.
3604053.name: Dead Kennedys

3604548.bio: Underground hip-hop group formed in Philadelphia in the early 90s by Stoupe and Vinnie Paz. Known for dark, horrorcore-tinged lyricism and records like The Funeral and the Raven (2021).
3604548.name: Jedi Mind Tricks

3609536.bio: Noah Lennox, member of Animal Collective, whose solo work layers reverb-soaked Beach Boys-like harmonies over sample-based production. Albums include Person Pitch (2007), Reset (2022) and Sinister Grift (2025).
3609536.name: Panda Bear

3611366.bio: Austin psych-revival band conjuring dark, moody psychedelia with garage rock and shoegaze touches. Albums include Passover (2006), Phosgene Nightmare and Wilderness of Mirrors (2022), and they founded the Levitation festival.
3611366.name: The Black Angels

3614038.bio: Upstate New York duo Sarah Barthel and Josh Carter, mixing hip-hop-inspired beats with dreamy electronic pop. Albums include Eyelid Movies (2009), Voices (2014) and Three (2016).
3614038.name: Phantogram

3614044.bio: UK ensemble led by drummer Malcolm Catto, hard to pigeonhole, blending psych, jazz, funk, hip-hop and library music. Albums include Out There (2007), Infinity of Now (2020) and Legna (2023).
3614044.name: The Heliocentrics

3618024.bio: Grammy-winning Mexican singer-songwriter and producer, with a stylistically wide catalogue from pop to folk and traditional Latin American music. Albums include Hasta la Raiz (2015), De Todas las Flores (2022) and Cancionera (2025).
3618024.name: Natalia Lafourcade

3619685.bio: Sweet Trip is a San Francisco group blending indie pop, shoegaze and electronica. Their lush Velocity : Design : Comfort (2003) is a cult classic, and they returned with A Tiny House in Secret Speeches (2021).
3619685.name: Sweet Trip

3624326.bio: Oxford shoegaze pioneers who married extraterrestrial guitar tones to songs about cars and restlessness. Raise (1991) and Mezcal Head (1993) are classics, with a return via I Wasn't Born to Lose You (2015) and Future Ruins (2019).
3624326.name: Swervedriver

3625314.bio: Large Los Angeles collective formed in 2007 around Alex Ebert, born from the recording of Up From Below (2009). Their communal, gospel-tinged folk-rock produced the hit Home; later albums include Here (2012) and PersonA (2016).
3625314.name: Edward Sharpe & The Magnetic Zeros

3630984.bio: Garage-psych power trio formed by Ty Segall with Charles Moothart and Chad Ubovich, worshipping 1960s proto-metal and fuzz. Albums include Fuzz (2012), II and III.
3630984.name: FUZZ

3632680.bio: Florida band from Jacksonville, known for atmospheric progressive, post-rock-leaning alternative rock. Releases include Dreamhouse (2010), Young and Courageous (2014) and Every Nothing (2018).
3632680.name: Tides Of Man
3632680.note: Bio from hints and general knowledge; no Tidal bio, not verified by search

3633240.bio: Boston band formed in 1990, part of the city's chimp rock scene pitting dreamy guitar sounds against noise. Albums include Blonder Tongue Audio Baton (1993) and They Spent Their Wild Youthful Days in the Glittering World of the Salons (1996).
3633240.name: Swirlies

3633298.bio: Argentine rock legend, frontman of Soda Stereo, the most influential rock en espanol band, and later a solo artist with an ambitious electronic-tinged style. Records include Amor Amarillo (1993) and Bocanada (1999). He died in 2014 after years in a coma.
3633298.name: Gustavo Cerati

3637822.bio: Stephen Wilkinson, a producer and multi-instrumentalist from Wolverhampton, England, who blends folk, electronic, hip hop and rock into warm, atmospheric collages. Early records such as Hand Cranked (2006) were lo-fi, and later albums such as BIB10 (2022) and Phantom Brickworks (2024) refined the pastoral sound on Warp.
3637822.name: Bibio

3638338.bio: Kurt Vile is a Philadelphia singer-songwriter and guitarist who began in The War on Drugs. His laid-back, loping indie rock is heard on Smoke Ring for My Halo (2011), Wakin on a Pretty Daze (2013) and b'lieve i'm goin down... (2015).
3638338.name: Kurt Vile

3638894.bio: Gothenburg indie band whose dramatic, punk-tinged indie pop is powered by Maja Milner's powerful vocals. Albums include Makthaverskan II (2014), Ill (2017), För Allting (2021) and Glass and Bones (2026).
3638894.name: Makthaverskan

3641069.bio: Rock supergroup of Josh Homme, Dave Grohl and John Paul Jones, who began discussing it in 2005 and unveiled it in 2009. They released one self-titled album (2009) of heavy, groove-driven alternative rock.
3641069.name: Them Crooked Vultures

3642059.bio: Southern California band known for the "Sweater Weather" beach anthem, mixing moody 90s alt-rock and pop with hip-hop and electronics. Early work includes I'm Sorry... (2012) and I Love You. (2013).
3642059.name: The Neighbourhood

3642161.bio: Mexico City band formed in 1986 around Saul Hernandez, a leading name in Latin American alternative rock. Gothic-tinged albums like El Silencio (1992) and El Nervio del Volcan (1994) made them rock en espanol classics.
3642161.name: Caifanes

3642854.bio: Brooklyn synth-rock trio started in 1998 by Jon Philpot, then in Atlanta. They mix psychedelic, electronic and indie rock textures with big hooks. Key records include I Love You, It's Cool (2012) and Time Is Over One Day Old (2014).
3642854.name: Bear In Heaven

3643826.bio: Indie rock band from Ridgewood, New Jersey, helping establish the warm, hazy jangle style of the late 2000s. Albums include Real Estate (2009), Days (2011), Atlas and Daniel (2024).
3643826.name: Real Estate

3644153.bio: San Diego noise-pop duo of Charles Rowell and Brandon Welchez, mixing noise and melody in neon-lit, hooky songs. Early albums such as Summer of Hate (2009) were fuzzy and fully formed; Upside Down in Heaven (2023) and Greetings from Hell (2026) continue it.
3644153.name: Crocodiles

3644492.bio: Los Angeles band led by Cory Hanson, starting as spooky psychedelic garage rock and evolving to classic-rock and pop influences. Records include Golem (2015), Laughing Matter (2019) and Vertigo (2024).
3644492.name: Wand

3644905.bio: Philadelphia band led by Domenic Palermo, blending heavy guitar walls with shimmering shoegaze. Albums include Guilty of Everything (2013), Tired of Tomorrow, Dance on the Blacktop and When No Birds Sang (2023).
3644905.name: NOTHING

3652908.bio: Duo of The Shins' James Mercer and producer Danger Mouse. Their self-titled 2010 debut and After the Disco (2014) blend Mercer's melodies with cinematic, retro-leaning production, with a third record, Into the Blue, in 2022.
3652908.name: Broken Bells

3653487.bio: New Zealand-born, San Francisco-based Tamaryn draws on lush 1980s-90s dream pop and shoegaze. The Waves (2010) had a hypnotic shoegaze churn, followed by Tender New Signs (2012), Cranekiss (2015) and Dreaming the Dark (2019).
3653487.name: Tamaryn

36578015.bio: Houston singer and project blending hypnotic shoegaze atmospherics with sludgy alt-metal riffs. Went viral with "Scars" (2023) from Vol. 1, followed by Dear Diary (2024) and VOL. 3 (2026).
36578015.name: Novulent

3660775.bio: Art-rock quartet formed in Edinburgh by art school friends, nominated for the Mercury Prize with their 2012 self-titled debut. They mix krautrock rhythms, synths and surf-like harmonies. Later records include Born Under Saturn (2015) and Off Planet (2023).
3660775.name: Django Django

3660776.bio: Project of Cameron Mesirow, based in Los Angeles, mixing dreamy experimental pop with layered electronics and personal themes. Records include Ring (2010), Interiors (2013) and crux (2023).
3660776.name: Glasser

3666541.bio: Project formed in 2000 by Mazzy Star singer Hope Sandoval with My Bloody Valentine drummer Colm O Ciosoig. A slow, hushed, folky dream pop sound, heard on Bavarian Fruit Bread (2001) and Until the Hunter (2016).
3666541.name: Hope Sandoval and the Warm Inventions

3667948.bio: Brooklyn indie band founded in 2004 as a solo lo-fi project by Jeremy Earl, growing into a respected psych-folk group. Albums include At Echo Lake (2009), Bend Beyond (2012) and Perennial (2023).
3667948.name: Woods

3668549.bio: Instrumental trio from Chicago combining sprawling post-rock with heavy metal-like riffs. Albums include Station (2008), Empros (2011) and Gnosis (2022).
3668549.name: Russian Circles

3669345.bio: British singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Croydon, first known for her vocals on Tricky's Maxinquaye. Her solo records include Quixotic (2003), The Blue God (2008), Some Place Simple (2010) and Forever I Wait (2021).
3669345.name: Martina Topley-Bird

3669865.bio: Pioneering garage band from Lima, Peru, active 1964-1966, whose raw, shouting songs like Demolicion are often cited as an early form of punk. Their recordings were compiled on Demolicion! The Complete Recordings (2010).
3669865.name: Los Saicos
3669865.note: Tidal bio missing; bio from general knowledge and hints

3685562.bio: Swedish stoner and fuzz rock trio from Örebro, formed in 2003, playing heavy rock with progressive leanings. They went on hiatus in 2013 and returned in 2015; records include II (2010) and III (2016). The Tidal entry also lists a trance compilation, likely a mismatch.
3685562.name: Asteroid
3685562.note: Tidal profile has no bio and includes a Future Sound of Egypt trance compilation; identified as Swedish band Asteroid from albums II and III

3689166.bio: London producer Aaron Jerome mixing dubstep, garage, house, soul and techno into bass-heavy, melodic electronic music. Known for singles like "Wildfire", collaborations with singers and albums such as The Rat Road (2023).
3689166.name: SBTRKT

3691667.bio: Minneapolis collective assembled around Ryan Olson, built on a 69-bpm slow-jam template. Their only album, Relayted (2010), blends smooth R&B, soft rock and indie pop with a rotating cast including Justin Vernon.
3691667.name: Gayngs

3699412.bio: English funk and dance-soul band, the Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland duo expanded to a collective. Busy Earnin' broke through in 2014 with their self-titled album; later records include Volcano (2023) and Sunshine (2026).
3699412.name: Jungle

3705930.bio: Jack Tatum's project from Virginia, begun in 2009 as shimmery synth-washed indie pop. Gemini (2010), Nocturne and Indigo lead to Hold (2023).
3705930.name: Wild Nothing

3707455.bio: DJ and producer born in South Africa and raised in Switzerland, making bright, sunny deep house with acoustic touches like flute and piano. Known for Come with Me and the Homebound EP (2019).
3707455.name: Nora En Pure

3708736.bio: Henry Laufer from Los Angeles, a founding member of the Wedidit Collective, makes experimental hip hop shaped by R&B, doom metal and drum'n'bass. Bad Vibes (2011) mixed airy beats with grim guitars; later work includes Dark Red (2015) and Repulsor (2025).
3708736.name: Shlohmo

3708743.bio: London electronic duo of Dominic Maker and Kai Campos, considered pioneers of post-dubstep before moving into left-field songcraft with guests like King Krule and James Blake. Records include Crooks & Lovers (2010), Cold Spring Fault Less Youth (2013), Love What Survives (2017) and The Sunset Violent (2025).
3708743.name: Mount Kimbie

3722866.bio: Los Angeles band blending psych-rock, post-punk, dream pop and hip hop into a smoldering style. After the 2008 EP Exquisite Corpse, The Fool (2010) and Warpaint (2014) followed, with Radiate Like This (2022).
3722866.name: Warpaint

3725096.bio: This Will Destroy You are a Texan post-rock band from San Marcos, writing lengthy atmospheric instrumentals with shoegaze and ambient influences. Key records include Young Mountain (2008) and Tunnel Blanket (2011).
3725096.name: This Will Destroy You

37322.bio: Oxford indie rock band that emerged in the late 2000s with a spiky mix of math rock, new wave and atmospheric post-rock. Antidotes (2008) reached the UK top three. Later albums include Holy Fire (2013) and the two-part Life Is Yours (2022).
37322.name: Foals

3736815.bio: Tame Impala is the project of Australian multi-instrumentalist Kevin Parker, from Perth. He moved from psychedelic rock to synth-heavy pop. Key records include Lonerism (2012), Currents (2015) and The Slow Rush (2020).
3736815.name: Tame Impala

3753399.bio: Los Angeles singer-songwriter and composer blurring indie music, modern composition and electronics. Key records include Tragedy (2011), Have You in My Wilderness (2015) and Aviary (2018).
3753399.name: Julia Holter

3753433.bio: Cleveland indie rock band led by Dylan Baldi, who began as a teenage lo-fi bedroom project. Driving, urgent albums such as Here and Nowhere Else (2014) and Attack on Memory (2012) are their best known.
3753433.name: Cloud Nothings

3767613.bio: London indie pop band that produced reverb-heavy songs full of melody, co-ed harmonies and hints of darkness. Over five years they released Veronica Falls (2011) and Waiting for Something to Happen (2013).
3767613.name: Veronica Falls

3767614.bio: Brooklyn indie band led by Dustin Payseur, known for chiming reverb-soaked guitars and easygoing songwriting. Their 2010 self-titled debut was a defining record of the dreamy indie wave alongside Wild Nothing and DIIV; later albums include Somersault (2017) and Bunny (2023).
3767614.name: Beach Fossils

3767618.bio: Project of Shaun Kilfoyle from New York, offering moody indie pop that drew comparisons to The Cure, New Order and My Bloody Valentine. Albums include By the Hedge (2011) and Tides End (2013).
3767618.name: Minks

3767624.bio: Belfast group that began as noisy indie pop on Slumberland and evolved through shoegaze into darker post-punk and synth textures. Albums include Dead to Me, The New Life and Stains on Silence (2018).
3767624.name: Girls Names

3768703.bio: New Jersey-born singer-songwriter, based in Brooklyn, writing hushed, intense songs that range from indie folk to darker synth sounds. Albums include Epic (2010), Are We There (2014) and Remind Me Tomorrow (2019).
3768703.name: Sharon Van Etten

3781920.bio: Japanese band from Kobe, formed around 2006, playing emotional noisy shoegaze-tinged indie rock. Records include No New World (2018) and Awakening:Sleeping (2022).
3781920.name: MASS OF THE FERMENTING DREGS
3781920.note: No Tidal bio; identification from hints and background knowledge

3783424.bio: Frontwoman of the Yeah Yeah Yeahs who also works solo and on soundtracks. Her debut album Crush Songs (2014) was lo-fi balladry, followed by Lux Prima (2019) with Danger Mouse.
3783424.name: Karen O

3795582.bio: Melodic project of Justin Broadrick (Godflesh), merging heavy riffs with ambient textures and pop-minded structures. Self-titled debut (2004), followed by records such as Silver (2006) and Pity / Piety (2022).
3795582.name: Jesu

37989811.bio: Alias of New York singer-songwriter chloe mk, making lo-fi shoegaze dreamscapes mixed with acoustic minimalism. Debut All the Same All OK came out in 2021.
37989811.name: sweet93

3816041.bio: Compton rapper celebrated for lyricism, concept albums and mainstream success. Landmarks include good kid, m.A.A.d city (2012), To Pimp a Butterfly (2015) and GNX (2024).
3816041.name: Kendrick Lamar

3816948.bio: Noise-rock quartet from Devon, based in Bristol, mixing shoegaze, drone, indie rock and post-punk. Albums include Hindsight (2021) and AM DRAM (2024), meant to be their last.
3816948.name: Spectres

3819025.bio: Swiss singer-songwriter Fabian Sigmund from Zurich. His music runs from psychedelic rock and blues to Americana and folk, and from Veränderet (2022) onward he sings in Zurich German. Other releases include Sad and Horny (2016) and fäderliecht (2025).
3819025.name: Fai Baba

3819688.bio: Claire Boucher, Canadian artist from Vancouver who produces her own futuristic pop. Halfaxa (2010) and Visions (2012) mixed dream pop, R&B, electronic and hip hop, and Art Angels (2015) and Miss Anthropocene (2020) followed.
3819688.name: Grimes

3824.bio: Hit-making British synth pop duo of Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith. The Hurting (1983), Songs From the Big Chair (1985) with Everybody Wants to Rule the World, and The Tipping Point (2022) are their key works.
3824.name: Tears For Fears

3832155.bio: Chilean-American producer born in New York, known for experimental, reflective downtempo indebted to jazz, modern classical and minimal techno. Space Is Only Noise (2011) was his debut; later work includes Sirens (2016) and Piedras releases.
3832155.name: Nicolas Jaar

3835736.bio: Dream pop project of Brooklyn bassist Katy Goodman (Vivian Girls), later shifting toward punk and alt-country. Albums include La Sera (2011), Sees the Light (2012) and Music for Listening to Music To (2016).
3835736.name: La Sera

3835737.bio: Project of Montreal artist Jasamine White-Gluz, which began as a doomy shoegaze duo at the end of the 2000s and grew steadily more experimental. Albums include Ghost Blonde (2010), Wait to Pleasure (2013), More Faithful (2015), Motherhood (2020) and Bugland (2025).
3835737.name: NO JOY

38429689.bio: Alt-rock project fronted by Amy Gonzalez from Boise, Idaho, whose song I Don't Care gained over 64 million streams. Her debut album Lover of a Ghost came out in 2025 on Mom+Pop.
38429689.name: Violent Vira

3850668.bio: Los Angeles band with an ever-evolving muscular and mind-altering sound, a wry humour and a mystical aesthetic. Aenima (1996), Lateralus (2001) and Fear Inoculum (2019) are landmarks.
3850668.name: TOOL

3854660.bio: Instrumental progressive metal trio led by guitarist Tosin Abasi, formed in Washington DC around 2007 and releasing records from 2009. Known for virtuosic eight-string guitar work and djent-leaning rhythms; The Joy of Motion (2014) and Parrhesia (2022) are key albums.
3854660.name: Animals as Leaders

3855757.bio: Solo project of Matthew Mondanile, founding guitarist of Real Estate, from New Jersey. Hazy, sunlit guitar pop and psychedelia across Landscapes (2009), Arcade Dynamics, The Flower Lane and later records.
3855757.name: Ducktails

3855761.bio: Chilean psychedelic duo of Ives Sepúlveda and Manuel Parra from Santiago, rising in the early 2010s. Their drifting, sometimes bluesy sound is heard on Noctuary (2012) and Bolero Tampoco (2024).
3855761.name: The Holydrug Couple

3860530.bio: Russian alternative band from Rostov-on-Don formed in 2009, releasing a self-titled album (2010) and Другое за другим (2021). They sing in Russian and play dreamy, post-punk-tinged indie.
3860530.name: Utro
3860530.note: Details from one aggregator source; genre inferred from limited info
